meta.title: Flexible budgets and direct-cost variances
meta.summary: Static budgets and the static-budget variance, flexible budgets and the sales-volume and flexible-budget variances, standard costs, direct materials and direct labor price and efficiency variances, journal entries, and using variances.

videos.title: Static budgets and variances
videos.take: A variance is actual minus budget; favorable variances raise income, unfavorable ones lower it

scenes.say: Last month didn't go to plan. Variances tell managers by how much, and where to look.

sub: favorable (F) raises income, unfavorable (U) lowers it
scenes.say: A variance is the difference between an actual result and a budgeted amount. A favorable variance, marked F, increases operating income. An unfavorable variance, marked U, decreases it.

scenes.heading: Standard utility trailer, per unit
scenes.say: Prairie Gate's standard sixteen-foot utility trailer sells for $5,000. Its budgeted variable costs: five hundred pounds of steel at three dollars, a $1,000 kit of axles and lights, twenty-four hours of labor at thirty dollars, and variable overhead of ten dollars per labor hour. Contribution margin: $1,540.

scenes.heading: March: static budget vs actual
scenes.say: The March static budget was forty trailers and $21,600 of operating income. Prairie Gate actually built and sold thirty-six, and earned $14,590. The static-budget variance is $7,010 unfavorable.

sub: Fewer trailers explain some of it;
scenes.say: That single number isn't very useful. Some of the shortfall is because fewer trailers were sold; some is about prices and efficiency. The flexible budget separates them.

scenes.q: Actual direct labor cost $27,900; budgeted $28,800. Variance?
scenes.say: Quick check. Actual direct labor twenty-seven thousand nine hundred; budget twenty-eight eight hundred. Variance? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A. Spending less than budget is favorable: $900 F. But we'll see that comparison isn't fair, because fewer trailers were made.

videos.title: The flexible budget
videos.take: The flexible budget uses budgeted prices and costs at the actual output, splitting the static-budget variance

scenes.say: To compare fairly, budget for the output actually achieved. That's the flexible budget.
A flexible budget uses budgeted selling prices and budgeted costs per unit, but the actual output: what the budget would have been if Prairie Gate had planned thirty-six trailers.

scenes.heading: Three columns, March
scenes.say: The flexible budget for thirty-six trailers shows revenue of $180,000, variable costs of $124,560, fixed costs of $40,000, and operating income of $15,440.

scenes.heading: Splitting the $7,010 U
scenes.say: The sales-volume variance, flexible minus static, is $6,160 unfavorable: four fewer trailers times $1,540 of contribution. The flexible-budget variance, actual minus flexible, is only $850 unfavorable. That's what managers controlled through prices and costs.

These answer different questions. The sales-volume variance is mostly for marketing: why did we sell four fewer trailers? The flexible-budget variance is about prices and efficiency, which we break down next.

scenes.q: Budgeted CM $1,540; 4 fewer trailers sold than planned. Sales-volume variance?
scenes.say: Quick check. Budgeted contribution is fifteen forty per trailer, and four fewer were sold. Sales-volume variance? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Standard costs
videos.take: Standards set the expected quantity and price of each input per unit of output

scenes.say: To break the flexible-budget variance down, you need standards: what each trailer should use, and what each input should cost.

sub: or quantity, per unit of output
scenes.say: A standard is a carefully determined benchmark: the quantity of each input a unit should use, and the price each input should cost. Prairie Gate's standard is five hundred pounds of steel at three dollars, and twenty-four labor hours at thirty dollars.

scenes.heading: Setting standards
scenes.say: Ideal standards assume perfect conditions and are almost never met. Most companies use attainable standards: tight but achievable with efficient work, allowing for normal waste and downtime.

scenes.heading: Where standards come from
items: Benchmarks from other plants or firms
scenes.say: Standards come from engineering studies, past performance adjusted for improvements, benchmarks from other plants or companies, and supplier contracts for prices.

sub: Price variance: paid more or less per unit of input
Efficiency variance: used more or less input
scenes.say: With standards, each cost's flexible-budget variance splits into a price variance, paying more or less per unit of input, and an efficiency variance, using more or less input than the standard allows for the actual output.

scenes.q: Which standard most likely motivates welders?
opts: An ideal standard nobody has met
Last year's actual, whatever it was
scenes.say: Quick check. Which standard most likely motivates welders? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Attainable standards are challenging but reachable.

videos.title: Direct materials variances
videos.take: Price variance = (actual − budgeted price) × actual quantity; efficiency = (actual − standard quantity) × budgeted price

scenes.say: In March, Prairie Gate's steel cost $810 more than the flexible budget. Was it the price or the usage?

scenes.heading: Steel, March
scenes.say: Prairie Gate used eighteen thousand nine hundred pounds of steel bought at two ninety a pound: $54,810. The flexible budget for thirty-six trailers allows eighteen thousand pounds at three dollars: $54,000. The variance is $810 unfavorable.

The price variance is the difference between the actual and budgeted price, times the actual quantity: ten cents a pound below standard, times eighteen thousand nine hundred pounds, is $1,890 favorable.

sub: (Actual quantity − budgeted quantity for actual output)
scenes.say: The efficiency variance is the difference between the actual quantity and the quantity allowed for actual output, times the budgeted price: nine hundred extra pounds at three dollars, $2,700 unfavorable.

scenes.heading: Steel variances
scenes.say: Together: $1,890 favorable for price, $2,700 unfavorable for efficiency, $810 unfavorable in total. Cheaper steel, but more of it. Was it lower-grade steel that welded badly? That's the question for purchasing and production.

scenes.q: Actual 2,200 kg at $5.20; standard for actual output 2,000 kg at $5.00. Efficiency variance?
scenes.say: Quick check. Actual twenty-two hundred kilograms at five twenty; standard for actual output two thousand at five dollars. Efficiency variance? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A. Two hundred extra kilograms at the budgeted five dollars: $1,000 unfavorable.

videos.title: Direct labor variances
videos.take: Labor price (rate) and efficiency variances use hours instead of pounds

scenes.say: Labor works the same way. The input is hours, and the price is the wage rate.

scenes.heading: Direct labor, March
scenes.say: Welders and assemblers worked nine hundred hours at thirty-one dollars: $27,900. The flexible budget allows twenty-four hours per trailer, eight hundred sixty-four hours, at thirty dollars: $25,920. The variance is $1,980 unfavorable.

scenes.heading: Labor variances
scenes.say: The labor price variance: a dollar an hour over standard, times nine hundred hours, $900 unfavorable. The efficiency variance: thirty-six extra hours at thirty dollars, $1,080 unfavorable.

scenes.heading: Recording labor at standard
scenes.say: In a standard costing system, work in process is charged at standard: $25,920. Unfavorable variances are debits; favorable ones would be credits. Wages payable records what was actually owed.
Variances interact. The favorable steel price and unfavorable steel and labor efficiency may share one cause: cheaper, lower-grade steel that took more welding time and created more scrap.

scenes.q: Actual 520 hours at $29; standard for actual output 500 hours at $30. Price variance?
scenes.say: Quick check. Actual five twenty hours at twenty-nine dollars; standard for actual output five hundred hours at thirty. Price variance? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A. One dollar less per hour times five hundred twenty hours: $520 favorable.

videos.title: Using variances
videos.take: Investigate variances that are large or recurring, look for shared causes, and use them to learn, not to blame

scenes.say: Variances are only useful if someone acts on them. Here's how to use them well.

scenes.heading: March flexible-budget variance, $850 U
scenes.say: Here's the whole $850 unfavorable flexible-budget variance: a favorable price variance of $3,600, offset by steel, labor, variable overhead and fixed cost overruns. Overhead variances are next lecture.

scenes.heading: When to investigate
items: Size: large in dollars or percent
scenes.say: Not every variance needs investigating. Look at size, in dollars and as a percentage; trends, since a small variance that repeats every month matters; whether anyone can control it; and whether the benefit of investigating exceeds the cost.

sub: Who should explain the steel variance?
scenes.say: Used for blame, variances encourage gaming: purchasing buys cheap steel to win a price variance and production pays for it. Used for learning, they bring purchasing and production together to find the best total cost.
Standards can also be compared with external benchmarks, the best plants or competitors, to see whether Prairie Gate's attainable standards are actually competitive.

scenes.q: Purchasing earns a big favorable price variance on steel; production shows big unfavorable efficiency variances. What should management do?
opts: Investigate whether the cheaper steel caused the inefficiency
scenes.say: Quick check. Purchasing shows a big favorable steel price variance, and production big unfavorable efficiency variances. What should management do? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. They may share one cause, and the total cost is what matters.

warmup: You budgeted $400 for groceries for a month and spent $440, but you had house guests for a week. Did you overspend?
Not necessarily: a fair comparison adjusts the budget for the actual number of people. That's a flexible budget.
acts: April: 44 trailers sold at $4,950. Compute static (40 planned) and flexible budget operating income using the standard trailer data and $40,000 of fixed costs.
Explain why attainable standards are preferred to ideal standards.
Achievable with effort, so variances are informative and motivating; ideal standards guarantee unfavorable variances and discourage workers.
April steel: 22,600 lb purchased and used at $3.05. Standard 500 lb per trailer. Compute price and efficiency variances.
April labor: 1,030 hours at $29.50. Compute variances and record the journal entry.
Price (29.50 − 30) × 1,030 = 515 F. Efficiency (1,030 − 1,056) × 30 = 780 F. Dr WIP 31,680; Cr Labor price variance 515; Cr Labor efficiency variance 780; Cr Wages payable 30,385.
List three possible causes of an unfavorable labor efficiency variance and who would explain each.
Poor-quality steel (purchasing); new untrained welders (HR/production); machine breakdowns (maintenance); unrealistic standards (engineering/controller).
case: In March, purchasing switched to a new steel supplier offering $2.90 a pound, earning a $1,890 favorable price variance. Production complained that the steel had more mill scale, requiring extra grinding and causing more scrap. The purchasing manager's bonus is based on price variances; the plant manager's on efficiency variances.
Compute the combined effect on March costs of the steel switch, assuming all unfavorable steel and labor efficiency variances were caused by it.
Should Prairie Gate keep the new supplier?
What's wrong with the bonus system?

Price +1,890; steel efficiency −2,700; labor efficiency −1,080: net −1,890, about $52 a trailer worse. Return to the old supplier or demand quality improvements. Separate bonuses encourage each manager to win their own variance at the other's expense. Reward total cost per trailer, or joint purchasing–production targets including quality.
exam: Explain the difference between the static-budget variance, the sales-volume variance and the flexible-budget variance.

Static-budget variance = actual − static budget. It splits into sales-volume variance (flexible − static: effect of output differing from plan, at budgeted prices) and flexible-budget variance (actual − flexible: effect of prices and efficiency).
Standard: 3 kg at $8 per unit; 2 hours at $25. Actual for 1,000 units: 3,150 kg bought and used at $7.80; 1,950 hours at $26. Compute price and efficiency variances for materials and labor.
DM price 630 F; efficiency 1,200 U. DL price 1,950 U; efficiency 1,250 F.

ex.q: A variance that increases operating income is:
Budgeted CM $1,540 a trailer; 43 sold vs 40 planned. Sales-volume variance (positive if favorable)?
Actual OI $18,000; flexible-budget OI $20,500. Flexible-budget variance (negative if unfavorable)?
Steel: 19,500 lb bought and used at $3.10; standard $3.00. Price variance (negative if unfavorable)?
Steel used 19,500 lb; standard for actual output 19,000 lb at $3. Efficiency variance (negative if unfavorable)?
Labor: 780 actual hours; standard for actual output 800 hours at $30. Efficiency variance (positive if favorable)?
Which variance is most worth investigating?
opts: A $2,000 U variance recurring every month
ex.why: Size and trend matter; recurring variances signal a real problem.
